title: Video save: a saved recording IS the trimmed file
goal: Make video saving work exactly like image saving. Trim/crop were sidecar-only and 'applied at export', so the stored MP4 stayed full length and every consumer that hands out the file (drag from history, copy to clipboard) handed out the untrimmed original. Save must commit the edits into the stored asset, preserving the untouched original alongside so the edit stays reversible.

decisions.model: The stored media file is the TRUTH. Committing a save re-encodes the edits into it and preserves the pre-edit original in a hidden sibling folder (.photonz-originals/<same name>.mp4) so the .mp4 extension survives for AVFoundation and history never lists it. The .photonzedits sidecar changes meaning: it no longer describes pending edits to apply on the way out, it records how the visible file was derived FROM the preserved original — exactly the role the image editor's layered .photonz sidecar plays next to a flattened PNG.
decisions.editSource: The video editor always edits FROM the original when one exists (mirroring the image editor preferring its .photonz sidecar over the flattened PNG). So edits always compose against full-length source, repeated saves never stack, and resetting the trim + saving restores the full clip.
decisions.dirty: hasUnsavedChanges = exportEdits != committedEdits, where committedEdits = the sidecar's edits when an original is preserved, else none. That makes a legacy sidecar-only recording (trim recorded, file untrimmed) open as DIRTY, so the migration is a save prompt rather than silent loss.
decisions.consumers: Because the file is truth, the consumers stop applying edits: history poster/duration, copy-recording, and export-from-history all read the file verbatim. Only the editor's own Export/Copy still apply live unsaved edits, and they now read from the edit source, not the (already committed) media file.
decisions.testability: VideoExporter moved out of the SwiftUI app target into a new PhotonzMedia library (AVFoundation/ImageIO, no UI) with a PhotonzMediaTests target, so the regression test can synthesize an MP4, commit a trim, and read the stored asset's duration back.

tasks.title: Reproduce, and move video media IO into a testable PhotonzMedia target
tasks.notes: REPRODUCED both halves before changing anything. (a) Real user data: ~/Pictures/Screenshots/'Recording trim-ux-test.mp4' carries a .photonzedits sidecar saying keep 3.02s->12s, and the stored file is still 12s (mdls kMDItemDurationSeconds). CaptureStore.copyToPasteboard (history Copy) and CaptureThumbnailView.onDrag both hand out that file verbatim. (b) Statically: EditorCommands Save/Save As are .disabled(editor?.document == nil) and a video window publishes only videoEditorState, so Cmd-S is dead there; PhotonzApp attaches WindowCloseGuard to image windows only, so closing a video window with a pending trim never prompts. Codified as TrimSurvivesSaveReproTests (PhotonzMediaTests): a synthesized 3s clip + sidecar trim leaves the stored file at 3s, while VideoExporter.exportMP4 with the same trim already produces a correct ~1s file -- so the trim math exists and the job is routing Save through it. Moved VideoExporter.swift out of the app target into a new PhotonzMedia library (+PhotonzMediaTests) so the stored-asset promise is unit-testable; API made public, imports added to VideoEditorState/AppCoordinator/CaptureStore.

tasks.title: Core: original-preservation paths, commit planner, saved/dirty rule (TDD)
tasks.notes: New Sources/PhotonzCore/VideoSave.swift: VideoOriginals (hidden .photonz-originals sibling folder keeping the media extension so AVFoundation reads it and the capture scan skips it; editSource(for:) = original when preserved else the media file), VideoSaveState (committedEdits = sidecar ONLY when an original exists, else none -- which makes a legacy sidecar-only recording open dirty instead of silently losing the trim; needsSave with 1e-4s / 0.5px tolerance so float drift is not a dirty document), VideoCommitPlan + VideoCommitPlanner (source = original once preserved so trims never stack; originalToPreserve set exactly once; empty edits => requiresReencode false, a verbatim copy back from the original = revert to full clip). 14 tests in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/VideoSaveTests.swift, written first.

tasks.title: PhotonzMedia: commit edits into the stored asset, preserving the original (TDD; duration regression test)
tasks.notes: New Sources/PhotonzMedia/VideoAssetCommit.swift executes a VideoCommitPlan: build the new media into a dot-hidden scratch file inside .photonz-originals (same volume, invisible to the capture scan) via VideoExporter.exportMP4 (or a verbatim copy when the edits are empty), THEN preserve the pre-edit bytes, THEN FileManager.replaceItemAt so the recording keeps its name and creation date (history sorts by it), THEN write the sidecar. Any failure leaves the recording untouched. Tests (written first, Tests/PhotonzMediaTests/VideoAssetCommitTests.swift, 7): the regression that matters -- synth 3s clip, commit a 1s trim, read the STORED file back = ~1s; original kept at 3s in the hidden folder; a second, tighter trim measures against the original (~0.6s, not stacked); clearing the trim restores the full clip byte-for-byte and drops the sidecar; a crop commit changes the stored pixel size; name + creation date survive. TestClip.swift synthesizes real H.264 MP4s with AVAssetWriter.

tasks.title: Video editor saves like the image editor: Cmd-S, dirty dot, close confirmation, Save button, Revert to Original
tasks.notes: VideoEditorState: editSourceURL (= VideoOriginals.editSource, so the player and every edit measure against the original), committedEdits baseline recalled in loadMetadata, hasUnsavedChanges/canSave, save(completion:) building a VideoCommitPlan and running VideoAssetCommit off the main actor (then re-pointing the player at the newly preserved original via rebindPlayer, refreshing history, alerting on failure), revertToOriginal(). REMOVED the debounced persistEdits() sidecar writes -- 13 call sites -- because the sidecar must describe what the file HAS, not what is pending; unsaved trims are now protected by the close prompt instead of silently persisting. WindowCloseConfirmation gained a SaveableEditor protocol (hasUnsavedChanges/windowTitle/hostWindow/saveForClose(completion:)) that both EditorState and VideoEditorState conform to, so WindowCloseGuard, the edited dot, the Save/Cancel/Do-not-Save sheet and the Cmd-Q sweep work identically for video; save is completion-based because a video commit re-encodes. PhotonzApp attaches the guard + isDocumentEdited to video windows. EditorCommands: Cmd-S routes to video.save(), Cmd-Shift-S to the existing MP4 export panel (no new flow), Video menu gained Revert to Original. VideoEditorView: a Save icon button in the controller's edit cluster, shown when dirty, spinner while committing.

tasks.title: History: Show in Finder replaces the video Export menu
tasks.notes: User feedback 2026-08-22: "the export button on the history for video items - i don't understand it. I can understand a show in finder button." The video tile's Export menu (Export GIF... / Export HEIC..., a save panel that wrote a converted copy somewhere) is gone, replaced by a Show in Finder icon button -> AppCoordinator.revealInFinder. Rationale: a history item IS a file in a normal folder, so pointing at it is the useful answer; a FORMAT choice belongs in the editor's Export menu with the other format choices, which still has MP4/GIF/HEIC + quality. No capability lost -- Copy GIF is still on the tile's Copy menu. AppCoordinator.saveRecording(_ sourceURL:as:) had no other caller and was deleted.

tasks.title: Consumers read the stored file as truth (history thumbnail/duration, copy, export-from-history)
tasks.notes: Because the file is the truth, the edit-application code came OUT of the consumers rather than being added to more of them (the fix this task existed to reject): AppCoordinator.saveRecording(url:) and copyRecording(entry:) no longer load the sidecar; CaptureStore.loadVideoMetadata takes poster + duration straight off the file; VideoExporter.posterFrame lost its edits: parameter entirely. CaptureStore's cache-invalidation fingerprint moved from the sidecar to the MEDIA file (a commit rewrites it), and trashSidecar now also trashes the preserved original. The editor's own Export/Copy still apply live unsaved edits but read from state.editSourceURL, not state.url -- otherwise an export after a save would re-apply the trim to already-trimmed media. CaptureThumbnailView.onDrag and ClipboardWriter were NOT touched: they now work because the file they hand out is right.
